Fungal infection.description: A fungal infection is caused by fungi that can affect the skin, nails, or internal organs. Common types include ringworm, athlete's foot, and candidiasis.
precautions: Keep affected area clean and dry

Allergy.description: An allergy is an immune system response to a foreign substance (allergen) that is typically not harmful. Symptoms can range from mild to severe.
precautions: Wear a mask in dusty environments

GERD.description: Gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD) occurs when stomach acid frequently flows back into the esophagus, causing heartburn and irritation.

Chronic Cholestasis.description: Chronic cholestasis is a condition where bile flow from the liver is reduced or blocked, leading to accumulation of bile acids in the blood.

Drug Reaction.description: A drug reaction is an unwanted side effect or allergic response to a medication. Severity ranges from mild rashes to life-threatening anaphylaxis.
precautions: Inform your doctor about all reactions
Carry a list of drug allergies
Seek emergency care for severe reactions

Peptic Ulcer Disease.description: Peptic ulcers are open sores that develop on the inner lining of the stomach and upper small intestine, often caused by H. pylori or NSAIDs.
precautions: Avoid NSAIDs like aspirin and ibuprofen
Eat regular meals and avoid spicy food

AIDS.description: Acquired Immunodeficiency Syndrome (AIDS) is a chronic condition caused by HIV that damages the immune system and interferes with the body's ability to fight infections.

Diabetes.description: Diabetes mellitus is a metabolic disease characterized by high blood sugar levels over a prolonged period due to inadequate insulin production or response.
precautions: Follow a balanced diet low in sugar

Gastroenteritis.description: Gastroenteritis is inflammation of the stomach and intestines, typically resulting from bacterial or viral infection, causing vomiting and diarrhea.

Bronchial Asthma.description: Bronchial asthma is a chronic inflammatory disease of the airways causing recurrent episodes of wheezing, breathlessness, chest tightness, and coughing.
precautions: Avoid known triggers (dust, smoke, cold air)
Get regular check-ups with your pulmonologist

Hypertension.description: Hypertension (high blood pressure) is a condition where the force of blood against artery walls is consistently too high, increasing risk of heart disease and stroke.

Migraine.description: Migraine is a neurological condition causing intense, debilitating headaches often accompanied by nausea, vomiting, and sensitivity to light and sound.

Cervical Spondylosis.description: Cervical spondylosis is age-related wear and tear of the spinal discs in the neck, which can cause pain, stiffness, and nerve compression.
precautions: Avoid prolonged computer use without breaks
Use a supportive pillow while sleeping

Paralysis (Brain Hemorrhage).description: Brain hemorrhage is bleeding in or around the brain that can lead to paralysis, loss of consciousness, and other severe neurological deficits.

Jaundice.description: Jaundice is a condition where the skin and whites of the eyes turn yellow due to elevated bilirubin levels, indicating liver, gallbladder, or blood disorders.

Malaria.description: Malaria is a life-threatening disease caused by Plasmodium parasites transmitted through the bites of infected female Anopheles mosquitoes.
precautions: Eliminate stagnant water near your home

Chicken Pox.description: Chickenpox is a highly contagious viral infection caused by the varicella-zoster virus, causing an itchy rash with fluid-filled blisters.
precautions: Isolate the patient to prevent spread
Keep nails trimmed to avoid scratching

Dengue.description: Dengue fever is a mosquito-borne tropical disease caused by the dengue virus, characterized by high fever, severe headache, and joint pain.
precautions: Stay hydrated and monitor platelet count
Seek medical attention if bleeding occurs

Typhoid.description: Typhoid fever is a bacterial infection caused by Salmonella typhi, spread through contaminated food and water, causing prolonged fever and gastrointestinal symptoms.
precautions: Complete the full course of antibiotics
Drink only boiled or purified water
Get vaccinated if in endemic areas

Hepatitis A.description: Hepatitis A is a viral liver infection spread through contaminated food or water, causing inflammation and affecting liver function.

Hepatitis B.description: Hepatitis B is a viral infection that attacks the liver and can cause both acute and chronic disease, transmitted through blood and body fluids.
precautions: Don't share needles or personal care items

Hepatitis C.description: Hepatitis C is a viral infection that causes liver inflammation, sometimes leading to serious liver damage, primarily spread through contaminated blood.
precautions: Get tested if you received blood transfusions before 1992

Hepatitis D.description: Hepatitis D is a liver infection caused by the hepatitis D virus (HDV), which requires HBV to replicate. It's the most severe form of viral hepatitis.

Hepatitis E.description: Hepatitis E is a liver disease caused by the hepatitis E virus, mainly transmitted through contaminated water in areas with poor sanitation.

Alcoholic Hepatitis.description: Alcoholic hepatitis is liver inflammation caused by excessive alcohol consumption over a prolonged period, potentially leading to liver failure.
precautions: Join a support group for alcohol dependence

Tuberculosis.description: Tuberculosis (TB) is a bacterial infection caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that mainly affects the lungs but can also affect other parts of the body.
precautions: Complete the full course of DOTS therapy
Ensure good ventilation in living spaces

Common Cold.description: The common cold is a viral infection of the upper respiratory tract caused by rhinoviruses, characterized by runny nose, sore throat, and cough.
precautions: Avoid cold beverages and ice cream

Pneumonia.description: Pneumonia is an infection that inflames the air sacs in one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid, causing cough, fever, and difficulty breathing.

Dimorphic Hemorrhoids (Piles).description: Hemorrhoids (piles) are swollen veins in the lower rectum and anus, causing discomfort, pain, and sometimes bleeding during bowel movements.
precautions: Use sitz baths for pain relief

Heart Attack.description: A heart attack (myocardial infarction) occurs when blood flow to the heart muscle is blocked, usually by a blood clot, causing tissue damage.
precautions: Chew an aspirin if not allergic

Varicose Veins.description: Varicose veins are enlarged, twisted veins that usually occur in the legs due to weakened or damaged valves, causing pain and swelling.
precautions: Avoid standing or sitting for long periods

Hypothyroidism.description: Hypothyroidism is a condition where the thyroid gland doesn't produce enough thyroid hormones, leading to fatigue, weight gain, and depression.
precautions: Maintain a balanced diet with iodine

Hyperthyroidism.description: Hyperthyroidism is a condition where the thyroid gland produces too much thyroid hormone, causing rapid heartbeat, weight loss, and nervousness.

Hypoglycemia.description: Hypoglycemia is a condition where blood sugar drops below normal levels, causing shakiness, confusion, and in severe cases, loss of consciousness.
precautions: Inform people around you about your condition

Osteoarthritis.description: Osteoarthritis is a degenerative joint disease where the protective cartilage that cushions bone ends wears down, causing pain and stiffness.
precautions: Use hot/cold therapy for pain relief

Arthritis.description: Arthritis refers to inflammation of one or more joints, causing pain, swelling, and stiffness that can worsen with age.
precautions: Stay physically active with gentle exercises
Apply hot or cold packs to affected joints

Vertigo.description: Vertigo is a sensation of spinning or dizziness that occurs due to problems in the inner ear or brain, affecting balance and coordination.
precautions: Sit or lie down when feeling dizzy

Acne.description: Acne is a skin condition that occurs when hair follicles become plugged with oil and dead skin cells, causing pimples, blackheads, and whiteheads.
precautions: Wash face twice daily with mild cleanser
Avoid touching or picking at acne
Stay hydrated and eat a balanced diet

Urinary Tract Infection.description: A urinary tract infection (UTI) is an infection in any part of the urinary system, most commonly affecting the bladder and urethra.
precautions: Urinate frequently and don't hold urine
Complete the full course of antibiotics

Psoriasis.description: Psoriasis is a chronic autoimmune skin disease that speeds up the life cycle of skin cells, causing thick, silvery scales and itchy, dry, red patches.
precautions: Avoid triggers like stress and cold weather
Get regular sun exposure in moderation

Impetigo.description: Impetigo is a highly contagious bacterial skin infection forming red sores that rupture, ooze, and form a yellowish-brown crust.

COVID-19.description: COVID-19 is a respiratory illness caused by the SARS-CoV-2 virus, ranging from mild symptoms to severe pneumonia requiring hospitalization.
precautions: Monitor oxygen levels with a pulse oximeter
Seek emergency care if breathing difficulty worsens

Influenza.description: Influenza (flu) is a contagious respiratory illness caused by influenza viruses, causing fever, cough, body aches, and fatigue.
precautions: Rest and drink plenty of fluids
Cover mouth when coughing or sneezing

Anxiety Disorder.description: Anxiety disorder is a mental health condition characterized by persistent, excessive worry and fear that interferes with daily activities.

Depression.description: Depression is a mood disorder that causes persistent feelings of sadness, loss of interest, and can affect how you think, feel, and handle daily activities.

Kidney Stones.description: Kidney stones are hard deposits of minerals and salts that form inside the kidneys, causing severe pain when passing through the urinary tract.
precautions: Drink at least 2-3 liters of water daily
Avoid oxalate-rich foods if prone to calcium stones

Chronic Kidney Disease.description: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) is a gradual loss of kidney function over time, eventually requiring dialysis or kidney transplant in advanced stages.

Irritable Bowel Syndrome.description: IBS is a common gastrointestinal disorder affecting the large intestine, causing cramping, bloating, gas, diarrhea, and constipation.

Anemia.description: Anemia is a condition where you lack enough healthy red blood cells to carry adequate oxygen to your body's tissues, causing fatigue and weakness.
precautions: Eat iron-rich foods (spinach, lentils, red meat)
Include vitamin C to improve absorption

Epilepsy.description: Epilepsy is a neurological disorder characterized by recurrent, unprovoked seizures caused by abnormal electrical activity in the brain.
